subject: physics
title: Vectors, Scalars and the Projectile Launch
welcome_lead: Decompose motion into perpendicular components and predict where a projectile will land.
meta_desc: A-Level Mechanics adventure on vectors, scalars and projectile motion analysis.
final_note: Mastery of components turns 2D motion into two simple 1D problems.

concepts.def: Quantity with magnitude only, no direction.
Object moving under gravity only after launch.
Total time projectile spends in the air.

walkthroughs.body_html: A velocity v at angle theta to horizontal resolves into vx = v cos(theta) and vy = v sin(theta). These act independently.
Horizontal motion is uniform (no air resistance). Vertical motion accelerates downward at g = 9.81 m/s². Use suvat on each axis.
For a projectile launched from ground level, range R = v² sin(2 theta) / g. Maximum range occurs at 45 degrees.

options: Speed

mcqs.q: A projectile is launched at angle theta. Horizontal velocity component is:
options: v sin(theta)
v cos(theta)
v tan(theta)
v/cos(theta)

mcqs.q: For a projectile launched horizontally, what affects the horizontal component of velocity during flight (ignoring air resistance)?
options: The horizontal velocity increases over time because the projectile is falling.
Nothing — horizontal velocity stays constant; only vertical velocity changes due to gravity.
The lighter ball falls faster because it has less inertia.
Gravity slows down both the vertical and horizontal motion.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between mass and weight?
options: The horizontal velocity increases over time because the projectile is falling.
Mass is the amount of matter (kg); weight is the gravitational force on that mass (N) and depends on g.
Mass changes with location but weight does not.
Mass and weight are the same thing, just expressed in different units.

mcqs.q: If air resistance is ignored, which falls faster: a heavy ball or a light ball dropped from the same height?
options: The lighter ball falls faster because it has less inertia.
Both fall at the same rate because gravitational acceleration is independent of mass.
Mass changes with location but weight does not.
Heavier objects fall faster than lighter objects because gravity pulls more on them.
